text:
alyssa: Kicking off kythera-14b int4 canary this morning. Immediate failures on warmstart with batch_concurrency=3, max_new_tokens left at 512. OOMs look like KV prefetch + fragmentation.

alyssa: Sample error from node-12:
```
CUDA OOM: tried to allocate 1.1GiB for kv_prefetch buffer
 at serving/slots/allocator.cpp:198
```

tom: is this consistently reproduceable locally? sounds like slot allocator churn.

alyssa: yes repro on my mini canary cluster when sending long multi-turn sessions (context ~1400 tokens). Cold starts fine. Warmstart hits peak after a few requests.

priya: quick mitigations we can flip in model metadata: lower generation.max_new_tokens to 220, reduce batch_concurrency to 1-2, disable prefetch. Those are cheap.

marco: adding to that: increase slot_compactor_reserve from 0.01 -> 0.06 and lower kv_prefetch_window. On some models a larger reserve reduces fragmentation during KV growth spikes.

ops-bot: Patch apply request accepted for model kythera-14b-int4 @ canary-a: overrides queued.

alyssa: pushing config now:
```
model_overrides:
  generation.max_new_tokens: 220
  batch_concurrency: 1
  runtime.prefetch.enabled: false
  runtime.slot_compactor_reserve: 0.06
  runtime.kv_prefetch_window: 32
```

devops: note: changing batch_concurrency to 1 will reduce throughput; expect ~25% drop. We'll monitor latency and tail.

priya: also recommend running the bench script with warm-kv workload and instrumenting peak_gpu_mem per request. Link: https://internal.redwood/bench/kythera-warm-kv

marco: side note on quant: int4 shows a throughput win but we saw a small summarization quality delta in internal QA. We should compare fp16/int8/int4 on 2k prompt evals including multi-turn dialogues.

alyssa: queued a 2k eval set, focusing on long histories. Will include hallucination and ROUGE-L metrics.

ops-bot: Canary deploy started: kythera-14b-int4 @ canary-a at 6481260101

alyssa: early canary metrics (10m): avg_peak=11.6GiB, p95_peak=13.0GiB, OOMs dropped from ~6/100 -> 1/100 after overrides. Latency median +10ms, p95 +60ms.

priya: OOM rate improved but we need <0.1% before GA. If int4 can't hit that we fallback default to int8 for GA and continue int4 tuning.

marco: experiment idea: enable runtime.kernel_affinity=small-alloc and increase freelist_bucket_count. For some int4 kernels that reduces transient spikes.

devops: can we do staged routing? prefer int4 for dev and power customers, int8 for enterprise by default. Routing rules are easy to add.

alyssa: ran microbench and attached results (short summary): int4 token/sec +24% vs int8; int8 token/sec +7% vs fp16. Peak mem per warm request: int4=12.8GiB, int8=10.9GiB.

marco: interesting - int4 peak mem higher despite quantization because of prefetch patterns and temporary buffers. That explains frag + OOM.

priya: once evals are back we can make a call. If ROUGE-L int4 delta <-1.0 we should stop and use int8. If quality close and OOMs persist, try freelist tuning + slot compactor GC cadence.

alyssa: evals completed: int8 ROUGE-L delta vs fp16 = -0.05, int4 = -0.9 on summarization set; dialog F1 also slightly worse on int4.

devops: based on that, suggest GA with int8 default and keep int4 as experimental with strict runtime limits (no prefetch, batch_concurrency<=1, and routing tags).

marco: I'll open an infra ticket to add automated fallback routing when OOM_rate > 0.5% for a model variant. That keeps customers safe while we iterate on int4.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-kythera-int4-fallback-8721

alyssa: opening PR to set int8 as default for kythera and add a short troubleshooting playbook for int4: build flags, freelist knobs, kernel_affinity suggestion. PR: https://internal.redwood/pull/kythera-default-int8-456

priya: also add a brief note in the model-catalog: "kythera-14b defaults: generation.max_new_tokens=220 to mitigate warmstart KV fragmentation" so customers know.

alyssa: thanks team. We'll reconvene after infra implements fallback and Marco lands freebies. :white_check_mark:
